\begin{chapstatus}{The thread of this chapter}
A bit is a voltage inside a guaranteed range, and a gate is a few switches: the button of the kit is now a circuit you understand. Next: the machines built from gates.
\par\medskip\textbf{Exit ticket} (two to four minutes, alone, on paper):
\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=2em]
\item In two sentences: how does a MOS transistor act as a switch, and why does a CMOS inverter draw almost no current when its input is steady?
\item On the kit an input reads 1 above 2.475 V and 0 below 0.825 V; an output gives a 1 above 2.64 V. A wire adds 0.1 V of noise downwards. Can a 1 be misread? What does an input read at 1.6 V?
\end{enumerate}
\end{chapstatus}
